purpose: Identify the synchronous first Windows RTCPeerConnection constructor delay without joining or opening capture.
test: single fresh packaged renderer; no account, tracks, offer, SDP, capture or ICE gathering

native.clockHandling: Packet clock defaults and sequence-local incremental clock snapshots converted to nanoseconds before matching begin/end spans.

attribution: The renderer waits for the WebRTC signaling thread while the GPU process enumerates Media Foundation hardware video encoder profiles. GetSupportedProfiles occupies 994.7453 ms of the 1000.7 ms constructor. Actual PeerConnection::Create takes only 0.526 ms after capability discovery completes.
tracePrivacy: Fresh isolated profile, no account, non-loopback networking denied, netlog excluded, argument filtering enabled. This report omits trace arguments, GPU/device identities, process IDs and command lines; the raw trace was deleted after extracting the allowlisted timing evidence.
captureCategories: Electron getCategories() returned an empty array; this original capture used default categories with netlog excluded. The tracked reproduction explicitly selects webrtc/media/audio/gpu/toplevel/user-timing categories.
reproductionValidation: Tracked script syntax checked; tracked parser verified on the original capture. No second capture was run.
limitations: One hardware/environment observation; it identifies capability enumeration, not a particular codec, GPU, driver defect or universal Windows duration.
Asynchronous capability preparation remains a causal experiment until measured; this trace alone does not prove a successful remedy.
Moving the synchronous constructor earlier would move its main-thread pause rather than eliminate that work.
